      <title>Voldshendelse i Alta: To pågrepet av svensk politi</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/voldshendelse-i-alta_-to-pagrepet-av-svensk-politi--1.18087404</link>
      <description>To personer ble natt til mandag pågrepet av svensk politi i forbindelse med voldshendelsen i Alta søndag morgen, skriver politiet i loggen.
De to personene er bosatt et annet sted i Norge, siktet for drapsforsøk mot en mann bosatt i Alta.
Politiet etterforsker nå bakgrunnen for at de to dro til Alta og oppsøkte den fornærmede.
Etterforskningen så langt har avdekket at det har vært en relasjon mellom partene fra tidligere av.
Norsk politi vil be om at de siktede blir utlevert til Norge og vil framstille de for varetektsfengsling.</description>

      <description>Styret i Nvidia gjeninnsetter Jensen Huang som toppsjef i selskapet.
Avgjørelsen kommer etter samtaler og møter med Huang, opplyser selskapet i en pressemelding.
– I prosessen med å fatte beslutningen mottok styret innspill fra høytstående hold i den amerikanske regjeringen, og på bakgrunn av disse innspillene er styret trygg på at Huangs gjeninnsettelse ikke utgjør noen nasjonal sikkerhetsrisiko, heter det i pressemeldingen.
Nvidia-aksjen stiger 26 prosent i førhandelen.
For 11 dager trakk Huang seg etter en stor utroskapsskandale som involverte en mistenkt kinesisk spion.</description>

      <description>120 avviste asylsøkere i Danmark oppfyller kriteriene for å bli sendt til et retursenter i Rwanda neste år.

      <description>Karoline Grøtting var best av samtlige kvinner under dagens 15 kilometer fristil på Beitostølen.
5 kilometer før mål sto kampen om seieren mellom Grøtting og Kristin Austgulen Fosnæs. Der var det altså Grøtting som til slutt trakk det lengste strået.
Grøtting stod over fredagens 10 kilometer på grunn av magesmerter i et forsøk på å spare seg til dagens distanse.
– Jeg er veldig glad for det nå, sier Grøtting til NRK etter målgang.
Skiskytter Ida Lien var dagens andre startende og gikk i mål til ledelse. Der ble hun værende til Grøtting overtok lederstolen.
Likevel holdt det til 3. plass for skiskytteren.
Heidi Weng vant fredagens 10 kilometer klassisk, men klarte ikke å gjenskape prestasjonen i dag. Allerede ved 6,2 kilometer hadde Weng 17 sekunder opp til teten.
Weng endte på 5. plass, 36 sekunder bak vinner.
Herrene skal ut på sin 15 kilometer klokken 13:00. Den kan du følge på NRK TV.</description>

      <title>Selvik reddet straffe på overtid da Brest vant igjen</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/selvik-reddet-straffe-pa-overtid-da-brest-vant-igjen-1.18086449</link>
      <description>Egil Selvik fortsetter å storspille i Brest-målet. Lørdag sikret han 1-0-seier borte mot Strasbourg ved å redde straffespark fem minutter på overtid.
Sraffen ble dømt etter en VAR-gjennomgang av en situasjon der ballen traff armen til Brest-spiller Mama Baldé, men det berget ikke hjemmelaget.
Brest tok ledelsen ved Noah Edjouma i det 22. minutt, etter en svak klarering av keeper Filip Jørgensen. Selvik forsvarte ledelsen med en rekke gode redninger og hjalp laget sitt til den tredje strake seieren i Ligue 1.
Selvik voktet Norges mål i nasjonsligaseieren over Wales for en uke siden, men han måtte overraskende sette seg på benken igjen da Norge knep gruppeseieren med 3-2-seier over Danmark i Parken tirsdag. Da var Ørjan Nyland tilbake i målet. Lørdag satt Nyland på benken for RB Leipzig.
Brest-seieren løftet laget til 6.-plass på tabellen. Strasbourg har bare tre lag bak seg på tabellen.
(©NTB)</description>

      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/saudi-arabia_-har-skutt-ned-houthi-missiler-1.18086194</link>
      <description>Tre missiler som hadde retning mot Saudi-Arabias hovedstad Riyadh er skutt ned.
Det sier den saudiledede militærkoalisjonen, som er i en pågående væpnet konflikt med houthi-militsen.
I tillegg skal folk ha hørt flere eksplosjoner i Riyadh, melder Reuters.
Saudi-Arabia gikk til krig mot houthi-militsen i Jemen i 2015. Etter sju år med krig avtalte partene en våpenhvile i 2022.
I sommer har konflikten blusset opp igjen.</description>

      <description>Spillgiganten Rockstar Games knuser alle rekorder, melder Variety.
Allerede på lanseringsdagen omsatte «Grand Theft Auto 6», også kjent som «GTA 6», for 3,79 milliarder dollar.
Det tilsvarer over 37 milliarder norske kroner, og spillet forbigår dermed superheltfilmen «Avengers: End Game» som den største underholdningslanseringen noensinne.
«GTA 6» ble lansert torsdag på PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X og S, i tillegg til at det kan strømmes på Xbox One via Xbox Cloud Gaming.
I den sjette utgaven av actionspillet følger spillerne duoen Jason og Lucia mens de ufører ran og andre kriminelle oppdrag i den fiktive amerikanske delstaten Leonida.</description>

      <description>Norwegian har teke kontakt med rundt 5000 kundar og bede dei sperre bankkorta sine etter at ein leverandør til nettsidene deira er utsett for datainnbrot, melder NTB.

Hendinga er rapportert til Datatilsynet.

      <description>Et maleri av den nederlandske maleren Vincent Van Gogh er solgt for 190,4 millioner dollar.

The federal government has reversed its decision to pause some popular activities while reviewing its Canadian cadet and Canadian Ranger Group programs.

Last week, the Department of National Defence announced it was reviewing its financial plan for the program and several activities would be paused as it focused on reducing costs that do not directly support core activities and program delivery.

On Monday, the minister said the review was complete.

Watch the story below:

Loading the player...

“The Department of National Defence and the Canadian Armed Forces have now reviewed funding allocations and confirmed additional funding to support planned activities for the remainder of this fiscal year,” said Minister of National Defence David McGuinty.

The government did not say how much additional funding would be injected to support the programs by the end of the year.

McGuinty says participation has increased by 59 per cent throughout the last three years, a sign of its success, but also part of the reason budgets are stretched, and he says despite large increases in the national defence budget, there are many needs to balance.

“Every country in the world right now is trying to juggle needs, growth, equipment, international responsibilities, continental responsibilities here for us under NORAD, the Arctic; it’s not a limitless pot of support. So we have a responsibility to manage and deploy those resources responsibly and that’s exactly what we’re doing,” said McGuinty.

Member of Parliament for Nanaimo-Ladysmith Tamara Kronis, who said she spent a bunch of time at cadet-involved events in the riding over the weekend, was glad to see the reversal.

“All weekend, I was saying that I didn’t just want to see the minister back down but I wanted to see the minister back down before any activities were cancelled and this is the best result we could’ve hoped for,” said Kronis.

Kronis says she hopes cadets will learn from this moment.

“That when the government does something that negatively affects their lives that when they use their voices and act as a team that sometimes we can get those decisions reversed,” said Kronis.

A Campbell River father who’s working on a federal petition not just for a reversal but for expansion of the program has a more muted response.

“They’re basically just promising to restore what had already been scheduled and approved months ago, so I mean that’s great; however, why was this even the question in the first place?” said Grant Warkentin, whose two sons have been part of cadets.

Warkentin is calling on the government to work with cadet corps and support volunteer organizations to find long-term funding solutions to maintain programs and allow for future growth.

The minister wouldn’t make any funding promises past the fiscal year-end, March 31, meaning cadets and the rangers could be in limbo once again come spring.

A pop-up shop at The Bay Centre is selling forgotten items from hotel rooms across the province to raise money for Soap for Hope Canada.

The ‘Thrift for a Purpose’ pop-up shop, located on the mall’s lower level next to Centre Court, is selling unexpected hotel lost and found treasures that were left behind in hotel rooms at 70 of the organization’s partner hotels across B.C. and Alberta, including the Empress, Parkside and Oak Bay Beach Hotels.

Watch the story below:

Loading the player...

Angie Vinueza, with Soap for Hope Canada, says with the items coming from high-end hotels, there are plenty of treasures to find.

“So we have really good stuff like purses, coats, a lot of winter stuff,” Vinueza said. “We have found a really nice Giorgio Armani purse. We always get super surprised why people leave these wonderful treasures behind.”

Vinueza says the racks throughout the store are filled with everything from prom dresses to T-shirts and jeans. There are also displays showing off purses, hats, shoes and perfumes.

This is the fourth pop-up store Soap for Hope has set up in Victoria, this one being the first at The Bay Centre.

The law, passed by the NDP in 2023, was intended to force density into residential neighbourhoods as a solution for the housing crisis, but has been widely opposed by municipalities who say the one-size-fits-all attitude has led to inappropriate and unpopular developments in neighbourhoods.

“(It) created the reality of having fourplexes and sixplexes possible on any property, any single-family lot, regardless of whether there’s the infrastructure, the utilities to support it, no parking requirements, and really, I think we’ve seen right across British Columbia, it has been resisted by mayors and city councils,” he said.

Canadian icon Steven Page serves up a festive culinary favourite, crafting golden Holiday Latkes then lighting up the room with an iconic, signature performance of “Cheese Log” and “Brian Wilson”

Loading the player...

Holiday Latkes with Smoked Salmon & Homemade Apple Sauce

Apple Sauce

  • 4 lbs apples (peeled, cored, and chopped)
  • ⅓ cup water
  • 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
  • ½ to 1 tsp ground cinnamon
  • Sugar to taste (optional)
  1. Place the chopped apples, water, and lemon juice into a large saucepan or Dutch oven over medium heat.
  2. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and let it simmer for 15 to 25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the apples are very tender and falling apart.
  3. Remove the lid and stir in the cinnamon and sugar (if using).
  4. Remove from heat and use a potato masher for a chunky texture, or an immersion blender, food processor, or high-speed blender for a smooth puree.

Holiday Latkes

  • 1.5 to 2 lbs russet potatoes (peeled or unpeeled)
  • 1/2 medium yellow or white onion
  • 1 to 2 large eggs, lightly beaten
  • 2 to 4 tbsp matzo meal or all-purpose flour (plus an optional pinch of baking powder)
  • 1 tsp kosher salt and black pepper to taste
  • Neutral high-heat oil (such as canola, peanut, or vegetable oil) for frying
  1. Grate: Shred the potatoes and onion using the large holes of a box grater or a food processor grating disc.
  2. Drain moisture: Place the shreds in a clean kitchen towel or cheesecloth and squeeze out as much liquid as possible. (Tip: Let the drained liquid sit for a few minutes and scoop the settled white potato starch at the bottom back into your mixture for extra crispiness.)
  3. Mix batter: Stir the squeezed potatoes and onion together with the egg, matzo meal or flour, salt, and pepper until evenly combined.
  4. Heat oil: Pour about ¼ inch of oil into a heavy skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering (around 350°F–375°F).
  5. Fry: Drop heaping spoonfuls or ¼-cup scoops into the hot oil and flatten slightly with a spatula. Fry in batches without crowding for 3 to 5 minutes per side until deeply golden brown and crisp.
  6. Drain and serve: Transfer latkes to a paper towel-lined plate or wire rack, sprinkle with a pinch of salt while hot, and serve immediately with applesauce and/or sour cream with smoked salmon (or salmon roe).

A nationwide recall has been issued for several Cadbury chocolate products because they may contain undeclared pistachios, posing a potential risk to people with tree nut allergies.

The Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA) issued the food recall warning on Nov. 20, involving Cadbury Dairy Milk Oreo treat-size bars and two varieties of Cadbury Favourites chocolate collections.

The affected products may contain pistachios that are not listed on the ingredient labels.

The recall includes:

  • Cadbury Dairy Milk Oreo Candy (treat-size bar): Approximately 14.5 grams, with codes 2026 JA 3 and 2026 JA 4.
  • Cadbury Favourites: 45 Fun Treats Treat Size Bars: 498 grams (45 count), UPC 0 61200 01984 1. Affected codes include BV13126371, BV13126372, BV13126373, BV13226371, BV13226372, BV13226373 and BV13226376.
  • Cadbury Favourites: 90 Fun Treats Treat Size Bars: 993 grams (90 count), UPC 0 61200 01986 5. Affected codes include BV14926373, BV14926375 and BV14826372.

The CFIA says the recall was triggered by a consumer complaint, and one allergic reaction has been reported in connection with the consumption of the affected products.

People who have purchased the recalled products and have a tree nut allergy or sensitivity are advised not to consume them. The products should be thrown out or returned to the store where they were purchased.

Consumers are also being warned not to serve, use, sell or distribute the recalled products.

The recalling company is Mondelez Canada Inc. The CFIA is conducting a food safety investigation and says additional products could be recalled as a result.
